metaDescription: Five 5 inch random orbital sanders under $75, compared on orbit speed, dust collection, vibration control and the swirl marks cheap pads leave behind.
expertTake: The Bosch ROS20VSC is the pick for anyone sanding furniture or cabinet doors, because its pad dampening system is the one feature that actually reduces swirl marks on contoured and flat work. The DEWALT DWE6421K is the choice for long sessions, thanks to a separate counterweight that calms vibration. Skip a random orbital sander if you only touch up small trim, because a detail sander reaches corners that a round pad never will.
introParagraphs: A random orbital sander spins its pad in a circle while the pad also wobbles in a small orbit, so no abrasive grain follows the same path twice. That motion is what leaves a surface ready for finish instead of crossed with scratches, but the quality depends on the pad, the counterweight and how well the dust is pulled away.

This guide explains what a spending cap of $75 buys, what you give up compared with a pro sander, and which specs matter for swirl-free results. Our top picks are above, with full reviews below. Prices move, and the cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: Bosch ROS20VSC 5 in Variable Speed Random Orbital Sander
products.description:
The Bosch ROS20VSC is a 5 inch palm sander with a 2.5 amp motor and variable speed. Its standout feature is the pad dampening system, which stops the pad from spinning freely when you lift it off the work. A pad that keeps spinning when it touches down is the main cause of gouges and swirls, so a pad that brakes the moment you lift is a real quality feature.

Variable speed lets you drop the rate for finishing and raise it for stock removal. Because a random orbital sander cuts fastest at high speed and finest at low speed, a dial is more useful than a fixed-speed motor. Compared with the DEWALT DWE6421K, which has a 3 amp motor, the Bosch has less raw power but better pad control.

The hook and loop pad wears out after a year or two of regular use, so check that discs stay flat on it. Replace the pad when the hooks flatten, and use a vacuum on the dust port rather than relying on the small bag. A good routine is to let the sander reach full speed before you lower it, then lift it only after you have switched off and the pad has stopped. Even with dampening, pressing hard defeats the purpose, since the weight of the tool alone is enough pressure for a random orbital.
products.bestFor: Furniture, cabinet doors and any work where swirl marks would show.
pros: Pad dampening system stops gouges on lift-off and touch-down
Variable speed suits stock removal and fine finishing
2.5 amp motor balances power and control
Hook and loop attachment makes disc changes fast
cons: Less motor power than the 3 amp DEWALT
Small dust bag fills quickly on a large project
Pad wears out after a year or two of regular use

products.name: DEWALT DWE6421K 5 in 3 Amp Random Orbital Sander Kit
products.description:
The DWE6421K pairs a 3 amp motor with 12,000 orbits per minute, and its most useful feature is a separate counterweight. A counterweight balances the offset of the eccentric that drives the orbit, and a separate one means less vibration reaches your hand. Vibration is the reason your fingers go numb after an hour of sanding, so lower vibration is a real comfort feature.

The tool is also shorter than many palm sanders, which lets you get closer to the work and lean on the pad less. A 3 amp motor is the strongest in the group, so it holds speed when you push on a coarse disc. Against the Bosch, the DEWALT offers more power but no pad dampening, and the listing does not mention variable speed.

Replace the pad when the hooks wear, and use a shop vacuum on the dust port. DEWALT parts are widely stocked, which helps in year three when the pad or the switch needs replacing. If you sand a lot of vertical surfaces, such as cabinet faces, the shorter body also reduces wrist strain because your hand sits nearer the work. A kit version also helps because the contents usually include discs and a carrying bag.
products.bestFor: Long sanding sessions where vibration and fatigue matter.
pros: 3 amp motor is the strongest in this roundup
Separate counterweight reduces vibration and hand fatigue
Shorter body lets you work close to the surface
Widely stocked DEWALT parts and replacement pads
cons: No pad dampening system, so lift-off can leave a mark
Listing does not state variable speed
Higher price tier than the other corded picks

products.name: SKIL SR211601 5 in Random Orbital Sander with Cyclonic Dust Box
products.description:
SKIL's SR211601 offers a 2.8 amp motor at 13,000 orbits per minute with variable speed and a cyclonic dust box. A cyclone spins the dust against the wall of the box so heavier particles drop out of the airflow, which keeps the filter from clogging as fast as a bag. A cleaner filter keeps suction stronger for longer, and the box is easy to empty.

The tradeoff is pad control. It does not list a pad dampening system, so you need a light touch at lift-off and touch-down. Compared with the DEKOPRO, the SKIL has a stronger brand name and a better dust box, and against the Bosch it gives up the pad brake but offers more orbits per minute.

Expect to buy more discs, since the three-sheet starter pack is small. Empty the box often, tap the filter clean and replace the pad when it wears. Cyclonic boxes only work well when the filter is clean, so tap it out between grits and replace it when it stays gray after cleaning. Hook the box to a vacuum hose if the manufacturer's port allows it for the best of both worlds.
products.bestFor: Buyers who sand in a room with no shop vacuum and want a decent onboard dust box.
pros: Cyclonic dust box keeps the filter clearer for longer
Variable speed suits stock removal and finishing
2.8 amp motor at 13,000 OPM cuts quickly
Easy-empty box makes cleanup quick between grits
cons: No pad dampening system, so lift-off can mark
Starter pack has only three sanding sheets
Onboard box captures less than a vacuum hose

products.name: DCA 5 in 3.0 Amp Random Orbital Sander, 6 Speeds, 12,000 OPM
products.description:
The DCA sander pairs a 3 amp copper motor with six speeds from 4000 to 12000 orbits per minute and ten discs in the box. A speed range that low is useful for finishing, since a slow orbit leaves a finer scratch pattern, and a high speed removes stock quickly. Six speeds is more steps than a basic dial.

A 10 fluid ounce dust bag with a rubber seal helps keep dust out of the air, though a bag fills fast in heavy sanding. The tradeoff is brand support: DCA is a lesser known label, so parts and pads may be harder to find. Against the DEWALT, it has a matching 3 amp motor and a wider speed range, but less refined vibration control.

Use the ten discs for a first project, then buy a better disc assortment. Keep the bag empty and wipe the pad clean of dust. A wide speed range also lets you use the same sander for light paint scuffing at the low end, which is something a single-speed sander cannot do. Because the brand is unfamiliar, keep the packaging for the return window and test the pad for flatness on arrival.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a strong motor and many speed steps at a low price.
pros: 3 amp motor matches the DEWALT at a lower price
Six speeds from 4000 to 12000 OPM allow fine control
Ten discs included for a first project
Rubber seal on the dust bag reduces airborne dust
cons: Lesser known brand with limited parts support
Vibration control is less refined than the DEWALT
Small bag fills quickly in heavy sanding

products.name: DEKOPRO 5 in Random Orbital Sander, 2.5 Amp, 6 Speeds, 16 Discs
products.description:
DEKOPRO gives you the largest disc assortment, with 16 discs from 60 to 1000 grit, a 2.5 amp motor reaching 14,000 rpm and six variable speeds. A grit range this wide covers rough stripping at 60 and fine finishing at 400 or above, so you can start a project without a trip to the store.

The detachable dust box is easy to empty, and a hook and loop pad makes disc changes fast. The tradeoff is power and refinement: a 2.5 amp motor is below the DEWALT and DCA's 3 amps, and the listing does not mention pad dampening or a counterweight. Against the Bosch, the DEKOPRO has more speeds and discs but less control at lift-off.

Use the high grits sparingly, since a 1000 grit disc is for polishing, not sanding. Keep the dust box empty and replace the pad when it wears. Since 16 discs cover a lot of ground, sort them by grit in a zip bag so you do not waste a coarse disc on finish work. A sanded surface should feel smooth at each grit before moving to the next, and the wide assortment makes that easy.
products.bestFor: Beginners who want a full disc assortment included.

Six speeds with a top speed of 14,000 rpm
Detachable dust box is easy to empty
Hook and loop pad changes discs fast
cons: 2.5 amp motor is below the 3 amp saw-class picks

buyingCriteria.explanation: Swirl marks come from a spinning pad touching down or lifting off, from too much pressure and from skipping grits. The Bosch's pad dampening stops the pad on lift-off, which is the single best swirl preventer in this group. For furniture and cabinet doors, this feature is worth more than extra motor power. Dampening costs little to include, so its absence on the other four is a real compromise, not a technical limit.

A counterweight balances the orbit so less shake reaches your hand. The DEWALT lists a separate counterweight design, which reduces fatigue in long sessions. Numb fingers after an hour is the classic sign of a vibrating sander. A heavier tool is not always smoother, so judge vibration by how your hand feels after ten minutes, not by weight.

A 3 amp motor holds speed under pressure, and 2.5 amps is enough for finishing. The DEWALT and DCA offer 3 amps, the SKIL 2.8 and the Bosch and DEKOPRO 2.5. Orbit speed of 12,000 to 14,000 OPM suits most work. Do not buy on amps alone, since a 3 amp motor with a poor counterweight still shakes.

Dust on the surface leaves scratches, and dust in the air hurts your lungs. A vacuum hose on the port beats an onboard bag, and a hole pattern that matches the disc matters. The SKIL has a cyclonic box, and the DCA has a sealed bag. Match the hole pattern on the disc to the pad, because a misaligned disc blocks the holes and drops suction.

Discs are the main running cost. The DEKOPRO ships 16 discs and the DCA ships 10, while the SKIL ships 3. Hook and loop discs from major brands fit all five, but match the hole pattern. Aluminum oxide discs last longer on hardwood than cheap paper discs, so buy a mixed pack for your first project.

A speed dial lets you slow the orbit for finishing and raise it for stock removal. The Bosch, SKIL, DCA and DEKOPRO have variable speed, and the DEWALT listing does not mention it. A fixed high speed on finish work leaves swirls. Use low speed for the last pass at 180 or 220 grit, since high speed at fine grit makes heat, not finish.

specDecoder.meaning: How many times the pad completes its small orbit each minute. Higher OPM cuts faster but leaves a coarser scratch, so a variable dial gives you both.
specDecoder.watchFor: The SKIL's 13,000 and DEWALT's 12,000 OPM differ less than the pad quality does.

specDecoder.meaning: Current draw indicates motor size. A bigger motor holds speed when you press.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DEWALT and DCA at 3 amps lead the Bosch and DEKOPRO at 2.5.

specDecoder.meaning: The size of the pad's orbit, often 3/32 to 3/16 inch. A larger orbit cuts faster but leaves a rougher surface, so finishing sanders use smaller orbits.
specDecoder.watchFor: Most listings omit it, so assume a small orbit in this price tier.

specDecoder.meaning: A fabric-like pad that holds discs without glue. It allows fast disc changes.
specDecoder.watchFor: The hooks wear flat, and discs then fly off.

specDecoder.meaning: The size of the abrasive particles, with lower numbers cutting faster and rougher. A typical wood sequence runs 80, 120, 180 and 220.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DEKOPRO's 1000 grit discs are for polishing, not for wood.

maintenance.why: A worn pad lets discs fly off mid-sand and scratch the work. A fresh pad holds discs firmly and gives an even finish.
A full bag blocks airflow and leaves dust on the work, and it also overheats the motor. Empty it often and tap the filter clean.
Dust in the vents raises motor temperature. Compressed air keeps it cool.
A clogged disc burns the surface. A fresh disc cuts cooler.
A nicked cord is a hazard. Replace damaged cords.

faq.q: Do I need a random orbital or a sheet sander?
faq.a: A random orbital leaves fewer swirl marks and removes stock faster. A sheet sander suits flat finishing and corners, and many shops own both for different stages.

faq.q: What does $75 buy in a random orbital sander?
faq.a: A 5 inch corded palm sander with a 2.5 to 3 amp motor. You give up brushless motors and extra pad refinement. The cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

faq.q: Why do I get swirl marks?
faq.a: Usually the pad touched down while spinning, the pressure was too high or you skipped a grit. Lift the sander only after the pad stops, and let the tool weight do the work.

faq.q: Which grit should I start with?
faq.a: Start at 80 for rough wood, then 120 and 180. Do not skip more than one step.

faq.q: Is an air sander a better choice?
faq.a: An air sander is lighter and cheaper, but it needs a compressor that supplies enough airflow, and the compressor noise adds up. For most homes, a corded electric sander is easier.

faq.q: Do I need a dust mask?
faq.a: Yes. Wear a dust mask and eye protection, and use a vacuum on the dust port. Fine wood dust is a health hazard, and some finishes contain lead in old homes.
